_comment: Each case pairs ONE objective with a fixed document set and states the determination a competent assessor would reach from those documents alone. `source` records where the case came from. external-review: the scenario and its expected determination come from an outside reviewer's reproduction, reported before the fix that addresses it — the engine was changed to satisfy the case, not the reverse. The document text is RECONSTRUCTED here to the review's description, because the reviewer's own files are not in this repository; what is independent of this implementation is the case, not the bytes. engine-repo: scenario, documents and label all written here, which tests what their author already believed and is weaker evidence. `expect` is satisfied | not-satisfied. `assessment_date` overrides the suite's date for a case that has to run on the date its review used. `rationale` is the argument for the label, and is the thing to dispute if you think a determination is wrong.

cases.rationale: Neither document establishes an awareness and training policy. One is about account monitoring, the other about authentication. The objective's generic words — policy, developed, documented — are all present and none of its subject matter is.

cases.rationale: The same reviewer's document, against the objective it actually addresses. Account use being monitored continuously, attributed to a role and a document section, with a dated scan, is what AC-2_g asks for. If this fails, the engine is refusing evidence that does the job.

cases.rationale: An awareness and training policy that is developed, documented, located in a numbered section, versioned and dated. This is the true positive the subject-matter rule must not break: a rule that refuses everything is not an improvement over one that accepts everything.

The organization-level security awareness and training policy is developed and documented in SSP section 12.1, version 2.4, dated 2026-01-15, and is disseminated to all personnel and roles with system access. The organization-level security awareness and training policy is developed and documented in SSP section 12.1, version 2.4, dated 2026-01-15, and is disseminated to all personnel and roles with system access. The awareness and training procedures are reviewed annually.

cases.rationale: Compliance vocabulary with no subject matter. Every word a policy document uses to describe itself is here — developed, documented, approved, reviewed, disseminated, consistent with applicable requirements — and nothing about accounts being monitored.

documents.name: boilerplate.txt
documents.text: The policy is developed and documented in accordance with applicable organizational requirements. It is reviewed and updated annually, approved by management, and disseminated to organizational personnel. The associated procedures are consistent with the requirements and are maintained by the organization.

cases.rationale: Evidence that says on its face it is not final. A draft marker means the organization has not yet asserted the control is in place, whatever the surrounding prose claims.

documents.name: draft-ssp.txt
documents.text: AC-2 Account Management. DRAFT — To be finalized. Account use is monitored continuously by the ISSO per SSP section 5.2. Most recent scan: 2026-05-28. TBD: confirm with the ISSO before submission.

cases.rationale: The same draft marker written with Cyrillic homoglyphs. A marker that can be spelled past the gate is not a gate. This case exists because the defence is cheap to write and cheap to lose.

documents.name: draft-ssp.txt
documents.text: AC-2 Account Management. DRАFT — Tо bе finаlizеd. Account use is monitored continuously by the ISSO per SSP section 5.2. Most recent scan: 2026-05-28.

cases.rationale: The objective asks whether accounts are created in accordance with defined criteria; the evidence says account creation requires documented approval and names the approver. Refusing this for the difference between 'created' and 'creation' would be a false negative produced by grammar.

documents.text: AC-2 Account Management. Account creation requires documented approval from the system owner and follows the account management procedures in SSP section 5.1, version 2.4, dated 2026-01-15. Account creation, modification and deletion are logged.

cases.rationale: Contingency planning and incident response are adjacent disciplines with overlapping vocabulary — plan, procedures, roles, testing, annual review. An incident response plan does not establish a contingency plan, and the overlap is exactly what makes this worth testing.

cases.rationale: No evidence at all. A determination of Satisfied from an empty corpus would mean the engine is not reading anything.

cases.known_limitation: Currently fails. The engine returns Other Than Satisfied because the retriever does not surface the paragraph that answers the objective, not because the document lacks it. Checked directly: running coverage over that paragraph alone gives 1.0. This is one of eight such objectives found when gate 2 was tightened in engine 1.2.0 — the previous rule concealed them by passing on generic vocabulary whatever passage it read. The case is here to hold the count visible rather than let it disappear into a green suite.
cases.rationale: The bundled CloudVault SSP states that the organization establishes conditions for group membership and assigns account managers by role. An assessor reading this document would find the objective addressed. A determination of Other Than Satisfied is a false negative — safer than the opposite, and still wrong.

documents.name: CloudVault-Federal-SSP.txt
documents.text:
SYSTEM SECURITY PLAN (SSP)
CloudVault Federal — FedRAMP Low Baseline
Version 3.2 | Effective Date: January 15, 2026
Last Reviewed: March 10, 2026

1. SYSTEM DESCRIPTION

CloudVault Federal is a cloud-based document management and storage platform
designed for federal agencies. The system processes, stores, and transmits
federal information classified at the FIPS 199 Low impact level.

System Owner: Jane Martinez, CISO
Authorizing Official: Robert Chen, AO
ISSO: Michael Torres

2. ACCESS CONTROL (AC)

2.1 AC-1: Access Control Policy and Procedures

CloudVault maintains a documented Access Control Policy (v3.2, approved
January 15, 2026). The policy addresses purpose, scope, roles,
responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational
entities, and compliance. The policy is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5
and applicable federal regulations. The access control procedures are reviewed
annually and updated as needed. Last review: March 10, 2026 by the ISSO. The
policy is disseminated to all system administrators and users via the
CloudVault intranet. Organization-defined frequency for policy review: at
least annually. Organization-defined personnel: ISSO, CISO, and System Owner.

2.2 AC-2: Account Management

The organization manages information system accounts by identifying and
selecting account types (individual, group, system, service); assigning
account managers (System Administrator and ISSO); establishing conditions for
group membership; requiring approval from the AO for account creation
requests; and creating, enabling, modifying, disabling, and removing accounts
per policy. Accounts are reviewed quarterly (organization-defined frequency:
quarterly). Inactive accounts are disabled after 30 days of inactivity.
Temporary and emergency accounts are automatically removed after 72 hours.

2.3 AC-3: Access Enforcement

The system enforces approved authorizations for logical access in accordance
with applicable access control policies. Role-based access control (RBAC) is
implemented using AWS IAM policies and CloudVault's permission engine. Access
decisions are enforced at the application layer (API gateway) and the
infrastructure layer (VPC security groups, NACLs). All access attempts are
logged per AU-2.

2.4 AC-7: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts

The system enforces a limit of 5 consecutive invalid logon attempts during a
15-minute period. After exceeding this threshold, the account is locked for 30
minutes. The ISSO is notified automatically via email.

3. AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY (AU)

3.1 AU-1: Audit and Accountability Policy and Procedures

CloudVault maintains an Audit and Accountability Policy (v2.8, dated February
2, 2026). The policy defines the audit requirements, log retention periods,
and responsibilities for audit review. Policy is reviewed annually by the ISSO.

3.2 AU-2: Event Logging

The following events are logged: successful and unsuccessful logon attempts;
account creation, modification, and deletion; access control changes;
privilege escalation; system startup and shutdown; and data export and bulk
download operations. Logs are maintained in AWS CloudWatch and forwarded to
the SIEM (Splunk Enterprise).

3.3 AU-3: Content of Audit Records

Audit records contain date/time, event type, user identity, source address,
outcome (success/failure), and affected resource identifiers. Records are
generated in JSON format with ISO 8601 timestamps.

4. CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT (CM)

4.1 CM-1: Configuration Management Policy

Not yet fully implemented. The configuration management policy is currently
being drafted. Target completion: Q3 2026.

4.2 CM-2: Baseline Configuration

The organization maintains a baseline configuration for the information system
using AWS Config rules and Terraform infrastructure-as-code. Baselines are
documented in the Configuration Management Database (CMDB). Baseline
configuration last updated: April 1, 2026.

5. IDENTIFICATION AND AUTHENTICATION (IA)

5.1 IA-1: Identification and Authentication Policy

CloudVault has an Identification and Authentication Policy (v2.5, effective
November 1, 2025). Reviewed annually by the CISO.

5.2 IA-2: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)

All users are uniquely identified and authenticated before access is granted.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for all privileged and
non-privileged users. Authentication mechanisms: SAML 2.0 federation with
agency IdP; TOTP-based MFA via hardware tokens or authenticator apps; and
PIV/CAC card authentication for on-premises access. Session timeout: 15
minutes of inactivity.

6. INCIDENT RESPONSE (IR)

6.1 IR-1: Incident Response Policy and Procedures

CloudVault maintains an Incident Response Plan (v1.9, dated December 15, 2025).
Organization-defined frequency for review: at least annually. Responsible
personnel: ISSO, CISO, Incident Response Team Lead.

6.2 IR-6: Incident Reporting

Security incidents are reported to the ISSO within 1 hour of discovery.
US-CERT notification occurs within the timeframes specified in FISMA reporting
guidance.

7. RISK ASSESSMENT (RA)

7.1 RA-5: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning

Vulnerability scanning is performed using Tenable Nessus (credentialed scans).
Scans are conducted monthly on all system components. Most recent scan: May
28, 2026. Critical findings: 0. High findings: 2 (remediation in progress
within SLA). Scan results are reviewed by the ISSO within 5 business days.

8. SYSTEM AND COMMUNICATIONS PROTECTION (SC)

8.1 SC-1: System and Communications Protection Policy

[TBD - To be finalized]

8.2 SC-7: Boundary Protection

The system implements boundary protection using AWS WAF at the edge; a VPC
with public and private subnets; network ACLs restricting inbound/outbound
traffic; security groups with least-privilege rules; and CloudFront CDN with
DDoS protection (AWS Shield). All traffic between system components uses TLS
1.2 or higher. External API endpoints require mutual TLS for agency
connections.

9. SYSTEM AND INFORMATION INTEGRITY (SI)

9.1 SI-1: System and Information Integrity Policy

Implementation is in progress. The policy framework has been developed but
formal approval and dissemination are pending.

9.2 SI-2: Flaw Remediation

The organization identifies, reports, and corrects information system flaws.
Patches are tested in a staging environment before production deployment.
Critical patches are applied within 30 days per FedRAMP ConMon.

cases.rationale: The reviewer's recheck of engine 1.2.0. Neither document says anything about a facility, a data centre, or who may enter one. The objective asks whether a list of individuals with authorized access to the facility where the system resides has been developed; account monitoring is not that list. The engine returned Satisfied at 74% support and 100% concept coverage because `access` is a word in PE-2's title and account documents are full of it. Run on 2026-09-11, the date the review used: on the suite’s own 2026-06-01 the document dates are in the future and the temporal gate refuses it, which would hide what this case is about.

After ambient `access` is set aside, PE-8's subject is physical, environmental, visitor, records — and "follow a documented approval workflow recorded in the ticketing system" matches `record`. A ticketing system is not a visitor log. cases.rationale: The other direction, and the guard against fixing a false pass by refusing everything. This document is what PE-2_a.[01] asks for: a named facility, a developed list of individuals authorized to enter it, an owner, and a review date. If the engine refuses this, the subject rule has been tightened past the evidence it exists to admit.

documents.name: physical-security.txt
documents.text: PE-2 Physical Access Authorizations. A list of individuals with authorized access to the Ashburn data center facility where the CloudVault system resides has been developed and is maintained by the Physical Security Officer. The facility access list is approved by the System Owner and reviewed quarterly. Physical access authorization credentials are issued to each individual named on the list, and individuals are removed from the facility access list within one business day when access is no longer required. Last review of the physical access list: 2026-05-30.
